record.paper_title: On the combinatorics of tableaux -- A notebook of open problems
record.original_question: Is the class of lattices that are isomorphic to a sublattice of the lattice of normal subgroups of some group self-dual?

evidence.quote: [Wor2024b, quest. 3.74] Is the class of lattices that are isomorphic to a sublattice of the lattice of normal subgroups of some group self-dual?

artifact.self_contained_problem: For a group $G$, let $\mathcal{N}(G)$ denote the lattice of normal subgroups of $G$, ordered by inclusion, with meet given by intersection and join by the subgroup generated by the union. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the class of all lattices $L$ such that $L$ is isomorphic to a sublattice of $\mathcal{N}(G)$ for some group $G$. The class $\mathcal{C}$ is said to be self-dual if for every $L \in \mathcal{C}$ the order-dual lattice $L^{\mathrm{op}}$ also belongs to $\mathcal{C}$. Determine whether $\mathcal{C}$ is self-dual.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a recent collection of open problems on tableaux combinatorics, citing it from a 2024 problem list. Web searches did not surface a published resolution. Related results (e.g., Chermak–Delgado self-dual sublattices, modularity of the normal subgroup lattice) do not settle the question. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Lattice of subgroups - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The lattice of normal subgroups of a group is modular; the Chermak–Delgado lattice is a self-dual sublattice of the subgroup lattice.
status_evidence.claim: Background results exist on self-duality of certain sublattices, but no general resolution of the stated question is indicated.
